_comment: Each entry records an invariant that CURRENT PM behaviour violates, with the
exact violation codes and counts produced by the canonical scenario seeded in
scripts/workflow-invariants-db-test.ts. That scenario is the only consumer:
counts are deterministic there, unlike a live database.
The suite is green only while observed == expected, code for code and count
for count. A new code is a regression; a code that stops firing is an
'unrecorded pass' and also fails. That second rule is deliberate: an Epic item
must delete its baseline entry in the SAME commit that makes the invariant
pass, so 'fixed' and 'recorded as fixed' can never drift apart.
WFI-001 has no entry — it already holds. Do not add one to silence it.

entries.note: PmChannelRun has no lease column and nothing expires an accepted run; it sits accepted forever.
An In Progress task still reads as 'being worked' off a stale accepted run that was never superseded.
recordPmChannelRunWorkflowAction settles the run complete for every action, including continuation-required ones such as start.
No disposition is recorded anywhere, so every terminal run is missing one.
A turn that produces no durable response and takes no workflow action still settles complete instead of interrupted.
A general flag_blocker stores only free prose; neither the external actor nor the requirement is structured.
createActionPlanSubtasksForTask scrapes Markdown headings and list items; approved plans carry no structured steps.
